variants.title: Kundt's tube: speed of sound in a steel rod
variants.sample: Steel rod, 1.00 m, clamped at the middle
variants.method: Dust figures in an air column
variants.unknown: the speed of sound in steel and its Young's modulus
variants.note: Steel is stiffer than brass, so the rod sings higher (about 2.5 kHz) and the dust heaps are closer together (about 6.9 cm). v = sqrt(Y / rho) with Y = 200 GPa, rho = 7850 kg/m3.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics / Engineering ToolBox: Young's modulus of steel about 200 GPa, density 7850 kg/m3; v = sqrt(Y/rho) for a thin rod

variants.title: Kundt's tube: speed of sound in a glass rod
variants.sample: Glass rod, 1.00 m, clamped at the middle
variants.method: Dust figures in an air column
variants.unknown: the speed of sound in glass and its Young's modulus
variants.note: Soda-lime glass is light and stiff (Y about 70 GPa, rho 2500 kg/m3), so sound runs through it faster than in brass. Stroke it gently with a damp cloth.

source.title: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics / Engineering ToolBox: Young's modulus of soda-lime glass about 70 GPa, density 2500 kg/m3; v = sqrt(Y/rho) for a thin rod
